context.whyNow: Treasury and Education launched the Defaulted Loans Support Center on September 30; explain the new online process and distinguish applying from leaving default.

opening.text: Borrowers with defaulted federal student loans have a new online route toward repayment.

evidence.quote: September 30, 2026. The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) and the U.S. Department of Education (ED) announced the launch of the Defaulted Loans Support Center, a new online portal that gives Americans with defaulted federal student loans a simpler way to understand their options, address default, and return to repayment.

body.text: Treasury and the Education Department launched a support center Wednesday.

evidence.quote: September 30, 2026. The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) and the U.S. Department of Education (ED) announced the launch of the Defaulted Loans Support Center, a new online portal that gives Americans with defaulted federal student loans a simpler way to understand their options, address default, and return to repayment.

body.text: It lets borrowers compare rehabilitation and consolidation, upload documents and track progress.

evidence.quote: Now, defaulted borrowers have a centralized portal to: Understand the consequences of default; Compare available paths out of default; Apply online for loan rehabilitation or consolidation; Make a payment on a defaulted loan; and Review repayment plans and loan-discharge options. Borrowers can also complete the loan rehabilitation application online, upload documents, review an estimated payment, electronically sign their agreement, and track progress without leaving StudentAid.gov.

closing.text: Applying is only the start. Borrowers still need to meet the requirements of their chosen path to leave default.

evidence.quote: Now, defaulted borrowers have a centralized portal to: Understand the consequences of default; Compare available paths out of default; Apply online for loan rehabilitation or consolidation; Make a payment on a defaulted loan; and Review repayment plans and loan-discharge options. Borrowers can also complete the loan rehabilitation application online, upload documents, review an estimated payment, electronically sign their agreement, and track progress without leaving StudentAid.gov.

Loan rehabilitation is a method of getting your federal student loan(s) out of default. You make a certain number of consecutive, on-time payments to ED or the guaranty agency (FFEL borrowers only) under a rehabilitation agreement. You must also sign a Rehabilitation Agreement Letter.

sources.title: U.S. Department of the Treasury and U.S. Department of Education Launch New Defaulted Loans Support Center
sources.excerpt: September 30, 2026. The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) and the U.S. Department of Education (ED) announced the launch of the Defaulted Loans Support Center, a new online portal that gives Americans with defaulted federal student loans a simpler way to understand their options, address default, and return to repayment. Now, defaulted borrowers have a centralized portal to: Understand the consequences of default; Compare available paths out of default; Apply online for loan rehabilitation or consolidation; Make a payment on a defaulted loan; and Review repayment plans and loan-discharge options. Borrowers can also complete the loan rehabilitation application online, upload documents, review an estimated payment, electronically sign their agreement, and track progress without leaving StudentAid.gov.
sources.reviewNote: Official September 30 release read in the web search index; direct web open was unavailable. Facts and announced features only, partisan claims excluded. No publication clock time is asserted.

sources.title: Student Loan Default and Collections: FAQs
sources.excerpt: Loan rehabilitation is a method of getting your federal student loan(s) out of default. You make a certain number of consecutive, on-time payments to ED or the guaranty agency (FFEL borrowers only) under a rehabilitation agreement. You must also sign a Rehabilitation Agreement Letter.
sources.reviewNote: Direct official borrower guidance read September 30. Use only the distinction between applying and satisfying requirements; older mail/fax instructions are superseded by the launch announcement and are not narrated.

sourceCheck.method: Read the full official Treasury release through its indexed web result; read the FSA quarterly update and borrower guidance directly.
limits: The announcement displays a date but no publication clock time. CNBC feed time is not the government's publication time.

Some FSA guidance still describes mail/fax and MyEdDebt. For the newly announced online process, the September 30 release takes precedence; detailed eligibility and implementation must be rechecked before a how-to treatment.
